concepts.def: The variety of all the different species of organisms on earth, or within an ecosystem.

concepts.term: Biodiversity and the stability of ecosystems
concepts.def: A great biodiversity ensures the stability of ecosystems by reducing the dependence of one species on another for food, shelter and the maintenance of the physical environment.

The future of the human species on Earth relies on us maintaining a good level of biodiversity. Many human activities are reducing biodiversity and only recently have measures been taken to try to stop this reduction.

concepts.term: Human population growth and standard of living
concepts.def: Rapid growth in the human population and an increase in the standard of living mean that increasingly more resources are used and more waste is produced. Unless waste and chemical materials are properly handled, more pollution will be caused.

Pollution can occur in water, from sewage, fertiliser or toxic chemicals; in air, from smoke and acidic gases; and on land, from landfill and from toxic chemicals. Pollution kills plants and animals which can reduce biodiversity.
Humans reduce the amount of land available for other animals and plants by building, quarrying, farming and dumping waste.

The destruction of peat bogs, and other areas of peat to produce garden compost, reduces the area of this habitat and thus the variety of different plant, animal and microorganism species that live there (biodiversity).
The decay or burning of the peat releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.
Large-scale deforestation in tropical areas has occurred to provide land for cattle and rice fields, and to grow crops for biofuels.
Levels of carbon dioxide and methane in the atmosphere are increasing, and contribute to 'global warming'.

concepts.term: Programmes to protect ecosystems and biodiversity
concepts.def: Scientists and concerned citizens have put in place programmes to reduce the negative effects of humans on ecosystems and biodiversity. These include: breeding programmes for endangered species; protection and regeneration of rare habitats; reintroduction of field margins and hedgerows in agricultural areas where farmers grow only one type of crop; reduction of deforestation and carbon dioxide emissions by some governments; recycling resources rather than dumping waste in landfill.

mcqs.q: What is meant by the biodiversity of an ecosystem?
options: The total number of individual organisms there
Number of different habitats found in the area
The number of species that depend on one another
The variety of the different species living there
mcqs.explain: Biodiversity is the variety of all the different species of organisms on earth, or within an ecosystem.

mcqs.q: A woodland has a great biodiversity. Why is this ecosystem more stable?
options: The number of individual organisms stays the same
Each species depends more on others for shelter
One species depends less on others for its food
The area contains a larger number of habitats
mcqs.explain: A great biodiversity ensures the stability of ecosystems by reducing the dependence of one species on another for food, shelter and the maintenance of the physical environment.

mcqs.q: As the human population grows, more untreated sewage and fertiliser drain into a river and many fish and plants die. What is the effect on the river?
options: There is no pollution as both are natural materials
Pollution kills organisms and biodiversity falls
Biodiversity is unchanged as fish numbers recover
Biodiversity falls but the ecosystem becomes stable
mcqs.explain: More waste is produced as the population grows, and unless it is properly handled more pollution is caused; pollution kills plants and animals which can reduce biodiversity.

mcqs.q: Part of an area of grassland is quarried for stone and the rest is ploughed to grow crops. What is the effect on other animals and plants?
options: Less land is available for other plants and animals
Quarrying reduces the land but farming does not
Biodiversity is unchanged as many individuals stay
The ecosystem is more stable once species are lost
mcqs.explain: Humans reduce the amount of land available for other animals and plants by building, quarrying, farming and dumping waste, which reduces biodiversity.

mcqs.q: A peat bog is drained and the peat is dug out and sold as garden compost. What are the effects?
options: The habitat is lost and carbon dioxide is released
Carbon dioxide is released by burning, not by decay
Biodiversity is unchanged as many organisms survive
The land stays available because it is not built on
mcqs.explain: The destruction of peat bogs to produce garden compost reduces the area of this habitat, and thus its biodiversity, and the decay or burning of the peat releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.

mcqs.q: A large area of tropical forest is cleared to grow crops for biofuels. What is the impact on biodiversity?
options: Biodiversity is unchanged because biofuels are renewable
Biodiversity falls when the cleared trees are burned
Biodiversity falls as the forest habitat is destroyed
Biodiversity falls, so the ecosystem becomes more stable
mcqs.explain: Large-scale deforestation in tropical areas, including clearance to grow crops for biofuels, removes the habitat and so reduces the variety of species living there.

mcqs.q: Levels of carbon dioxide and methane in the atmosphere are increasing. Which is a biological consequence of the global warming this causes?
options: Species die out where the air becomes much warmer
Some species change the areas where they are found
Areas near carbon dioxide sources are affected most
Ecosystems become more stable as species are lost
mcqs.explain: Biological consequences of global warming include loss of habitat, changes in the distribution of species and changes in migration patterns.

mcqs.q: A government wants to reduce the negative effects of humans on ecosystems and biodiversity. Which policy would have a positive impact?
options: Growing more crops that will be used to make biofuels
Spreading extra fertiliser on farmland each season
Digging up more peat bogs to sell as garden compost
Reducing deforestation and carbon dioxide emissions
mcqs.explain: Reduction of deforestation and of carbon dioxide emissions by some governments is one of the programmes put in place to reduce the negative effects of humans on ecosystems and biodiversity.
